Place
PLāS
n. (rendering Hebrew māqōm, Greek topos)
From Old French place, from Latin platea, a broad street or open space, ultimately from Greek plateia, broad. The Hebrew māqōm is built on the verb qūm, to stand or rise up — a place is where a thing stands. That derivation runs quietly under the biblical usage: a man's place is not merely where he happens to be but where he has been set, and the deepest question Scripture asks about place is who assigned it.

Biblical Definition

Place in Scripture is appointed, not stumbled upon, and the discovery that a place was appointed is one of the recurring surprises of the biblical narratives. Jacob, running for his life with a stone for a pillow, wakes to the recognition: “Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not” (Gen 28:16). He had chosen the spot for no reason but nightfall, and it turned out to be the gate of heaven. Moses is told that the ordinary desert under his feet is not ordinary: “the place whereon thou standest is holy ground” (Exo 3:5). Abraham's obedience is defined by the fact that the place was withheld from him — “when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went” (Heb 11:8) — faith being willingness to be placed by Another. For the wandering people of God the answer to placelessness is not a location but a Person: “Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations” (Psa 90:1), written by a man who had no fixed address for forty years. And the Lord Jesus makes the preparing of place His own present work: “In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you” (Joh 14:2). Over against every appointed place stands the terrible sentence at the end, where the earth and the heaven flee away and there is found no place for them — the one condition Scripture describes as worse than exile.

Webster 1828 Definition

A particular portion of space; a locality, spot, or region; a station, rank, or office assigned to a person; and in Scripture the appointed place of God's presence, the place prepared by Christ, and the dwelling place which God Himself is to His people.

expand to see more

PLACE, n. 1. A particular portion of space of indefinite extent, occupied or intended to be occupied by any person or thing.

2. Any portion of space, as distinguished from space in general; locality; situation; as the place of a battle.

3. Rank; order of priority or dignity; as, to take the first place in an assembly.

4. Office; employment; official station; as, to hold a place of trust.

5. In Scripture, the appointed spot of God's presence and worship. The place whereon thou standest is holy ground. Exod. 3. I go to prepare a place for you. John 14. Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place. Psalm 90.

Key Scripture

Genesis 28:16 — "And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not."

Exodus 3:5 — "And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground."

Psalm 90:1 — "A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations."

John 14:2 — "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you."

Modern Corruption

The place Christ went to prepare is dissolved into a state of mind or a symbol of acceptance, so that the plain promise of a prepared dwelling for a resurrected people is treated as too literal to be believed.

expand to see more

Joh 14:2 is regularly demythologised: the many mansions become a metaphor for spiritual security, and the going to prepare becomes a figure for the psychological comfort the disciples needed. The text resists this at every point. The Lord anticipates the objection Himself — if it were not so, I would have told you — which is a strange thing to say of a metaphor, and He grounds the promise in a bodily journey: I go, and I will come again, and receive you unto myself. The hope of the Christian is not absorption into a state but reception into a house by a Person who left in a body and returns in one. Where the place is spiritualised away, the resurrection of the body loses its point, for a bodiless soul needs no location; and the church loses the concrete future that has sustained its martyrs.

The opposite error is to make place everything — to invest a building, a city, or a plot of ground with the holiness that belongs to God's presence alone, so that pilgrimage to a site becomes a means of grace. The Lord settled this with the woman at the well: neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, shall ye worship the Father. Holy ground was holy because God was standing in it, and Jacob's stone was a gate of heaven because God was there, not because the stone possessed a quality. The principle to recover is that the presence sanctifies the place and never the reverse, which is why a persecuted congregation in a barn is standing on ground as holy as Horeb, and why the God who has been our dwelling place in all generations (Psa 90:1) cannot be left behind when His people are driven out of a country.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew māqōm is a place or standing-spot, from qūm, to rise or stand; it is the word for the place the LORD chooses to put His name. Greek topos is a place, spot, or opportunity, and gives the room prepared in the Father's house.

expand to see more

Hebrew māqōm (H4725) — place, standing-place, locality; from qūm, to arise or stand, so a place is where a thing stands.

Hebrew hammāqōm 'asher yibchar — the place which the LORD shall choose to put his name there (Deu 12:5); the appointed centre of Israel's worship.

Hebrew mā'ōn (H4583) — a dwelling or habitation; the word behind dwelling place in Psa 90:1.

Greek topos (G5117) — a place, region, or spot; also opportunity or room, as give place unto wrath (Rom 12:19).

Greek monē (G3438) — an abiding place, dwelling, mansion; the many mansions of Joh 14:2, from menō, to abide.

Usage

"Of a place discovered to be appointed: surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not (Gen 28:16)."

"Of God Himself as the believer's place: Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations (Psa 90:1)."

"Of the place Christ prepares: in my Father's house are many mansions... I go to prepare a place for you (Joh 14:2)."
